_comment: THE INCLUDE LIST for the local chess page, and the source of truth for what
it loads -- same contract as PaintProvider's modules.json (that folder's
README explains why: no candidate list, no directory scan, an edit here is
the whole of adding or dropping a provider). ChessProvider before
ShellProvider so the board's own globals exist before the navigator comes
up in the embedded terminal.
NetworkProvider IS here, and not because the page can serve anything -- it
cannot, there is no listening socket in a browser, and boot_chess.etcs's
HttpServer.Start says so in the terminal. It is here because the runtime on
this side of an address is meant to be the same runtime as on the other:
the hosted node is ChessProvider + NetworkProvider on Linux, so this page is
ChessProvider + NetworkProvider in a browser, same types, same verbs, same
boot-script shape -- the transport is the only thing the browser lacks. See
this folder's README, 'Name servers, all the way down'.
NO WindowProvider AND NO RenderProvider. Both are OPTIONAL and both are
left out on purpose -- see this folder's README, 'Why no canvas': the board
is DOM (a CSS grid of squares, exactly like the server-authoritative
chess.html this replaces), not a GPU surface, so there is no framebuffer
for either provider to own. ShellProvider's own page ships the same way
('and optionally WindowProvider.wasm' -- ShellProvider/scripts/www/README.md).
_scripts: Staged into the browser's filesystem by the page, under these names, before
main() runs -- so each one must also answer over HTTP (../serve_chess.etcs
mounts it). Just the one script: the whole board lives in one ChessNode, so
there is nothing here for a second script to wire up the way Paint's
_glue: The emscripten loader output. STAGED AS .js: served extensionless it
arrives as application/octet-stream, which the browser warns is not a
valid JavaScript MIME type, and it would land on the same name as the
NATIVE etcs binary in bin/. Naming it here rather than probing also
removes a guaranteed failed fetch on every load.
